references.text: Israel's weeping and lamentation after the spies' report, which is the background for the event in Deuteronomy 1:45
Parallel account of the people's grief and their attempt to go up into the land after the Lord's judgment
David cries out to the Lord but receives no answer - the same theme that God does not hear
God does not answer when people cry out, because they previously did not listen to him
The Lord hides his eyes and does not hear the people's prayers due to their disobedience
The Lord will not hear when the people cry out in distress, because they have turned away from him
God refuses to hear the people's cries and prayer because of their sin
The Lord hides his face and does not listen because the people have done evil
Because they did not listen when God called, he will not listen when they call
Esau found no room for repentance even though he sought it with tears - a parallel to Israel's weeping that was not heard
